title: getcheapapi: the cheapest route for SERP, X, keyword and backlink APIs
description: Open-source price router for paid data and media APIs. Prices every provider for a call, runs the cheapest, and refuses past your budget. Built for AI agents.
og_desc: Stop overpaying for data and media APIs. Quote first, then spend.
og_alt: getcheapapi: one call, five routes, priced before it runs.
eyebrow: Price router for paid data and media APIs.
h1: The API bill your agent never checks.
lede: SERP, X, Reddit, keyword volume, backlinks, images. getcheapapi prices every provider you can use for a call, runs it through the cheapest one, and refuses past your budget. Open source, runs on your machine.
fig1_aria: Figure: one call priced across five routes, stepping down from the failover price to the cheapest.
fig1_cap: one call, five routes, priced before it runs
r_h2: The same data costs up to 200× more. Depending on the route.
r_sub: Aggregators fail over to dearer sources without telling you. Options raise the price. Billing rules differ everywhere. Agents have no brakes.
big_cap: Price gap on one X search endpoint
led_foot: getcheapapi quote prints this before any run. It spends nothing.
f1_t: Ask for a capability, not a provider
f1_d: serp.google, x.search, keyword.volume, image.generate. Each maps to routes across providers, with field mapping and batching done for you.
f2_d: From a local cache: live price APIs where providers have them, published tables where they do not. Routes you hold no key for are priced too, so you see what another key would save.
f3_d: Fresh prices right before the call. AnyAPI is pinned to its cheapest source with failover off.
f4_d: Every run is estimated first and refused past --max-usd. The default cap is ten cents.
f5_d: Exit code 2 on a 402, and a stop on the first failure. An agent reads that as stop, not retry.
f6_d: When the cheapest price jumps, the run stops until you accept the new price.
f7_d: Inputs are deduped, and a list of queries runs as one batch where the provider allows it.
f8_d: Responses are saved and charges logged in ~/.getcheapapi. getcheapapi spend sums them by provider and endpoint.
f9_d: Image, video and speech generation via Yir, quoted before every job and capped server-side.
f10_d: Link the folder into Claude Code, Codex or another agent. From a clone it runs without installing the package.
fig2_aria: Figure: five routes for the same job as bars of decreasing height; getcheapapi runs the shortest.
fig2_cap: same job, five routes · getcheapapi runs the shortest bar
c_sub: Routes live in one catalog file. Prices and endpoints change, so a pull request is how a route gets added or fixed.
c_caption: Capabilities and the providers that serve them
i_h2: One install. No account. No markup.
i_sub: You pay providers directly, with your own keys. One key is enough to start.

a1: Yes. MIT licensed, no account and no fee. You pay providers directly with your own keys.
q2: Do I need a key for every provider?
a2: No. One key is enough. Routes you have no key for are still priced, so you can see what adding one would save.
q3: Does my data go through your servers?
a3: No. The price cache, ledger and saved results live in ~/.getcheapapi on your machine. The only traffic is the API calls themselves.
a4: Live where a provider has a price API, published tables where it does not. Every run re-prices right before it spends.
a5: No. LiteLLM and OpenRouter cover text models. getcheapapi is for paid data and media APIs.
q6: How do I add a provider or fix a price?
a6: Edit the catalog file, run the free schema check against the live provider, and open a pull request.
ft_tag: Open-source price router for paid data and media APIs. Quote first, then spend.
